title: Follow-up: Landry, the three-tune band, and Gaspard's name
summary: Henry Landry was the trumpeter in the kids' band that played two sheiks and the blues for gate receipts; Bigard cannot yet recall Gaspard's full name.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: One, you mentioned that when you first started playing in New Orleans that you played with somebody named Landry who played trumpet. What was Landry's first name?
Okay, and that was when you were just starting out?

Yeah. We were all kids together, just fooling around. And we used to -- every Saturday night we'd go find out who was giving a party or something and we'd play for the gate receipt. They'd charge them a quarter to come in, and so we'd wind up with about a dollar and a half or something like that for the whole night. And we had only about three pieces. 'The Sheik' was the main piece.
'The Sheik.' That's the same as 'the Sheik of Araby'?
Yeah, 'the Sheik of Araby.' And then the blues, and the third one was 'the Sheik'.
So we had two sheiks and the blues. That's all we could play, all night long.
Did Landry also become a professional musician?
And you and Landry worked with a drummer?

Yeah, we worked with -- I can't think of the drummer's name. We were all kids. I mean, we didn't pay much attention to anything like that. We was out for fun more than anything else, which we did have a lot of fun.
You mentioned that you went with Gaspar's big band. What was his full name?
His full name was -- oh, God.
Well, maybe we can come back to that.
We'll come back to that. I'll think of it.
